pages.text: A changing field drives a current: spin a coil of N turns in a field B and it gives ε = NBAω·sin ωt. Every generator works this way. The iron core that guides the field is built from thin $(item)Electrical Steel Laminations$(), so the changing field cannot stir currents inside it.

$(item)Magnetite$() comes from raw iron roasted with charcoal, or from the Spectrograph's radium assay. Pressed with clay and redstone it makes $(item)Ferrite Magnets$(): iron oxide that stays magnetised.

Iron is ferromagnetic because its atoms' spins line up by themselves - until a critical temperature, 1043 K for iron, shakes them apart. Above it the susceptibility is χ = C/(T − T_c). The item tag $(thing)ferromagnetic$() lists what a field pulls on, for the Magnetized effect to come.
